behaviorChanges: ensureAgentToken(workspace, agentId, grant?) no longer issues the constant four-scope set: without an explicit grant it derives the grant from the signed action policy (toolhub:intent/governor:check/receipt:verify iff the policy has at least one rule; toolhub:execute iff at least one rule has allowExecute; executeActionClasses = the classes whose rule allows execute) and throws AgentTokenGrantError, writing nothing, when the policy signature is missing/invalid.

Agent token meta is now v2: { v: 2, agentId, issuedTs, scopes, executeActionClasses, grantedBy }. An existing token keeps the scopes it was issued with even when the live policy later widens; issueAgentToken(workspace, agentId, grant) rotates under an explicit grant.

Legacy v1 meta (scopes only) reads as executeActionClasses [] with grantedBy { kind: 'legacy-unconditional' }: its scopes on disk are preserved, but a static-token execute is refused with a named reason until the token is re-issued (fail closed on upgrade).

POST /toolhub/execute: after the lease check and before toolhub.executeIntent, a request authenticated with a static token (auth.username === 'agent-token') is refused 403 `toolhub:execute does not cover action class <class>` when the token grant's executeActionClasses excludes the intent's actionClass; body carries refusedBy { kind: 'agent-token', metaPath, scopes, executeActionClasses, grantedBy } and widen (edit + re-sign .amc/action-policy.yaml, then re-issue the token). No approval, ticket or intent is consumed on refusal (asserted: sentinel absent, approval still QUORUM_MET). Admins, human sessions and lease-only agents are unaffected.

Scope refusals at /verify/receipt, /governor/check, /toolhub/tools, /toolhub/intent and /toolhub/execute keep the exact `missing scope <scope>` error string and, for static-token agents, add refusedBy and widen.

GET /agents fails closed per agent: when no valid signed grant exists the row carries agentTokenScopes: [] plus agentTokenRefusal (and agentTokenRefusedBy/agentTokenWiden) and no token file is written; successful rows gain agentTokenExecuteActionClasses and agentTokenGrantedBy.
findAgentByToken/readAgentToken return executeActionClasses and grantedBy alongside token/scopes (additive; agentCredentialAuth.ts unchanged and still typechecks).
studioAgentTokenPath and studioAgentTokenMetaPath are now exported from studioState.ts.
decisions: Worktree provisioning mismatch: the worktree was created at main (3d6b8d4a, 409 commits behind fa2ffac6, none of the Studio agent-auth work present). I ran `git checkout --detach fa2ffac6733fb67ee525f64c2da436365fa7f697` inside my own worktree only (no branch moved, no reset, no other worktree or .git internals touched). All work and every number here is against fa2ffac6; the diff is `git diff` in the worktree (uncommitted, detached HEAD).

The signed action policy (.amc/action-policy.yaml + .sig, verifyActionPolicySignature/loadActionPolicy) is the grant source for static tokens because it is the operator-controlled, signed artefact that already names allowExecute per action class; the mapping policy->scopes is recorded in the meta's grantedBy so a refusal can name it.

Lease-level granularity (WRITE_LOW vs WRITE_HIGH on a lease) is NOT implemented, and the exact reason is named in code, tests and refusal text: leaseScopeSchema in src/leases/leaseSchema.ts is a closed zod enum with no per-action-class execute scope, and src/leases is outside this track's write scope. A lease-only request is therefore decided by the governor's existing `action-policy-execute` condition alone (tested as an explicit boundary, not claimed as a guard). agentTokenGrantFromLease is provided (scopes = lease ∩ AGENT_TOKEN_SCOPES; execute classes from the signed policy with the reason recorded) for callers that mint tokens from a lease; nothing in src calls it yet.

Rule 7 proof that the new route guard is not decoration: M1 removed only the new check while the live policy allowed WRITE_LOW execute; the execute returned 200 with allowed:true and actually wrote the sentinel, i.e. the governor did not cover a token grant narrower than the live policy.

Widen text names what exists: edit the action policy rule, re-sign via signActionPolicy (there is no `amc policy action sign` verb; `amc policy action init` creates+signs and `verify` verifies), then remove the token/meta so GET /agents re-mints, or call issueAgentToken with an explicit operator grant. No new CLI was added (cli.ts is out of scope).

The /agents test scaffolds a second agent (token-scope-child) because getAgentPaths maps the legacy `default` agent to .amc/ itself and listAgents only reads .amc/agents/*, so `default` is never listed (same reason the AMC-1546 fixture uses a second agent).
apiDelegation.ts was not touched; nothing in it issues tokens or checks scopes.

Side effect observed and reverted: the 14-file batch run rotated the tracked fixture keys under .amc/keys/ (8 tracked files modified, 4 *.previous-* files created). Restored with `git checkout -- .amc/keys` and removed the untracked files; a rerun of studioNativeTaskService did not reproduce it, so it is attributable to one of the other 13 files but not pinned down (budget). Not caused by this track's changes.
blockers: Lease scope granularity (a `toolhub:execute:<class>` lease scope, verifier support, and lease issuance CLI/route) requires edits to src/leases/leaseSchema.ts, src/leases/leaseVerifier.ts and the /leases/issue route defaults — outside IMPL-2's write scope; hand to the leases track.

Not exercised: the full vitest suite, the release gate (mandatory profile), packaged/platform qualification, the `amc` CLI paths, gateway/proxy/wire/hook scopes, and any browser flow. A green run of the 14 named files is source qualification only.
result.reportMarkdown:
# IMPL-2 — Studio agent token scopes

**Commit** fa2ffac6733fb67ee525f64c2da436365fa7f697 (detached in worktree `/Users/sid/AgentMaturityCompass/.claude/worktrees/wf_3cc93fba-030-1`; the worktree had been provisioned at main 3d6b8d4a, 409 commits behind, so I detached my own checkout at the named commit — no branch moved, no reset, nothing outside the worktree touched).
**Environment** Darwin 25.6.0 arm64, Node v25.5.0, pnpm 10.33.0. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline` OK; `pnpm build` run only because `tests/studioNativeTaskService.test.ts` imports `dist/`.

## What changed
- `src/studio/studioState.ts` (222 → 345 lines): `AGENT_TOKEN_SCOPES`, `AgentTokenGrant`/`AgentTokenGrantSource`, `AgentTokenGrantError`, `agentTokenGrantFromActionPolicy`, `agentTokenGrantFromLease`, `issueAgentToken`, `agentTokenWidenText`; `ensureAgentToken(workspace, agentId, grant?)` derives the grant from the signed action policy when none is given and never widens an existing token; meta v2 records `executeActionClasses` + `grantedBy`; legacy v1 meta fails closed for execute classes; `readAgentToken`/`findAgentByToken` return the grant; token path helpers exported.
- `src/studio/studioServer.ts` (+110/−?): `scopeRefusal` and `agentExecuteClassCheck` helpers next to `hasScope`; the five `missing scope …` sites now return `refusedBy`/`widen` for static-token agents (error strings unchanged); `/toolhub/execute` refuses a static-token execute whose grant excludes the intent's action class after the lease check and before `executeIntent`; `GET /agents` fails closed per agent instead of minting under an invalid policy.
- `tests/studioAgentTokenScopes.test.ts` (new, 288 lines): 6 unit + 4 loopback-HTTP tests against the real Studio server, ToolHub, approvals and fs.write in a temp workspace.

## Results (all measured this run)
- New file: RED first (9 failed / 1 passed — the one pass is the lease-only boundary case, by design), then 10/10 green.
- 14 files (`studioAgentCredentialBinding`, `studioApiAuthorization`, `studioCliBridgeAuthz`, `studioNativeTask*` ×6, `cosProduct10*` ×4, new file): 142 passed, 10 skipped (dist-backed) before build; after `pnpm build` the 10 pass → 152/152, 0 failed.
- Typechecks: `tsc -p tsconfig.json` exit 0; `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` exit 0.
- Mutations: 6/6 went RED (see structured list). **M1** is the brief §2 rule-7 proof: with only the new route check disabled and the live policy allowing WRITE_LOW, the execute returned 200 `allowed:true` and wrote the sentinel — the governor's `action-policy-execute` condition does not cover a token grant narrower than the live policy.

## Named limitation
Execute-scope granularity is enforced on the **static token** grant (meta `executeActionClasses`). A **lease** cannot name an action class: `leaseScopeSchema` (`src/leases/leaseSchema.ts`) is a closed enum outside this track's write scope. Lease-only requests are decided by the governor's signed action policy alone; the test file asserts that boundary explicitly and the refusal/grant texts name it.

## Not exercised
Full suite, release gate, packaged/platform qualification, CLI paths, gateway/proxy/wire/hook scopes, browser. Side effect reverted: the 14-file batch rotated tracked `.amc/keys/*` fixtures (not this track's change; restored via `git checkout -- .amc/keys`; not attributed to a single file).

Tool calls used: about 47 of 150.
